newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO rangebound, Chinese demand steady.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO rangebound, Chinese demand steady.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Wednesday were assessed steady to a shade firmer but within the $117-$122 range, tracking gains on crude, traders said.
Traders said Chinese buyers have gradually emerged to buy fuel oil for December delivery. They said this would help to support prices in the near term.
Chinese trader in Hong Kong told Reuters that fuel oil output in China has decreased slightly as refiners produce more gasoil.
But supplies in the region remained adequate, traders said.
Late Wednesday, an offer was seen for 180-cst supplies loading in early December at $120.50 per tonne, slightly higher from offers at $120 seen on Tuesday.
Traders said Mideast supplies in December were expected to be normal.
KEDO has decided not to award its tender to import fuel oil for November, traders said.
Traders said KEDO has not provided any reasons for the decision and were unsure if KEDO would issue a tender to buy fuel oil again later this month.
In the swaps market, November fuel oil was quoted unchanged from Tuesday at $119.50/$120.50.
